## Claims
- [proved] Assume the integral \(q^r\)-box/Schur/Pieri presentation, with \(q=i+p\), \(r=j+c\), \(i,j\ge2\), \(p,c\ge1\), \(\min(p,c)=1\), and \(d=ij\). The eight lower-degree named slots are
  \[
  x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},
  \]
  \[
  \gamma,\quad x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})},\quad
  z=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)},\quad y_2=s_{(i^j,2)},\quad\theta,
  \]
  where \(\deg x_0=d\), \(\deg x_1=\deg y_1=d+1\), and every remaining nonzero slot has degree \(d+2\). Here \(i^0\) is omitted.
- [proved] The conditional definitions, including both boundary cases, are
  \[
  \gamma=
  \begin{cases}
  s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})},&p\ge2,\\
  0,&p=1,
  \end{cases}
  \qquad
  \theta=
  \begin{cases}
  s_{(i^j,1,1)},&c\ge2,\\
  0,&c=1.
  \end{cases}
  \]
  Indeed, \(s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})}\) lies in the \(q^r\)-box exactly when \(i+2\le q=i+p\), equivalently \(p\ge2\); and \(s_{(i^j,1,1)}\) lies in that box exactly when \(j+2\le r=j+c\), equivalently \(c\ge2\). Since \(\min(p,c)=1\), the allowed cases are \((p,c)=(1,1)\), \(p=1,c\ge2\), or \(p\ge2,c=1\); hence \(\gamma\) and \(\theta\) are never simultaneously nonzero.
- [proved] With these definitions, the lower-degree Pieri equalities are unambiguous:
  \[
  h_1x_0=x_1+y_1,\qquad
  h_2x_0=\gamma+z+y_2,
  \]
  \[
  h_1x_1=\gamma+x_2+z,\qquad
  h_1y_1=z+y_2+\theta.
  \]
  Each follows by adding respectively one box or a horizontal two-strip; a term outside the \(q^r\)-box is precisely replaced by \(0\) through the preceding conditional definitions.
- [proved] The requested standalone-restatement certificate is established, conditional only on the stipulated integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation. No parent-theorem conclusion is made.

## Strategy
Define every lower-degree class and encode the two box-boundary omissions by \(\gamma\) and \(\theta\).

## Gaps
No claim beyond this notation and boundary certificate is established.
